main_text.l: postquam nauigio aduecti fuissent ad intemperan-
tes Sirenes. Lacertis vero filium vinculis se constrin-
xisse, quasi carcere quodam incuitabili, significat
philosophiae secreta. Sirenas enim puto poesin fin-
gere informes ac turpes voluptates. & admiror ni-
mium in modum Homerum, commiscentem re-
bus veritatem, & cyceona nectare suaviorem audi-
tibus nostris instillantem, non secus ac revera no-
tham aquam vino alicui generosissimo miscoret.
sic enim neque fabulis fallemur, neque ininitain-[?]
comprehensibiliq; entium comprehensione men-
tem inebriabimus. quare per ceram quidem igno-
rantiam; per vinculum philosophiam intellexit.
inde solum Vlyssem, tam suavia, supra ipsos quoq;
cycnos audiuisse carmina fingit, & vinculis perru-
pisse viam. In malorum enim perspicuitate, cons-
titit virtus philosopha: in voluptatum vero fuga,
philosophiae é certamine comparatum tropæum.
Quoniam itaque, Antimache, Vlyssis errorem hæc
vita exprimit, ac in mare turbarum miser homo in-
natat, & circumstant nos Sirenorum[?] cantuum
voces, ventorum instar modo hinc modo alia no-
bis non bona intentant, Penelopeæ coniugem i-
mitabimur, firmum istud virtutum & diuinum
philosophiæ vinculum prætendentes.
Rubr. ANTHINUS AMPELINO, LXXXIII.
Appropinquat jam vindemia, & musto ebriosa
sunt acina. circumspicias igitur qua potes optimé
in via publica, & cretensem tibi canem adhibea-
s comitem. viatorum namque manus continentes

page.notes: Left margin: show-through from the other side of the leaf, and the edge of the neighbouring page, are not transcribed. The word "ininitain-" at the line end is doubtful, and the hyphen continues into "comprehensibiliq;". "Sirenorum" is doubtful: the print looks like "Sirencorum". "generosissimo miscoret" is doubtful for "miscceret" as printed. The rubric "Rubr." is printed and transcribed as it appears.
